chapters.summary: The Israelites multiplied greatly in Egypt, so the new king oppressed them with slavery and ordered the midwives to kill the Hebrew baby boys, but the midwives feared God and spared their lives.
keyPoints: The Israelites multiplied and grew strong, which frightened Egypt's new king.
The Egyptians increased their oppression, forcing the Israelites into hard labor.
The midwives feared God and defied the king's order, sparing the baby boys.
chapters.application: In the face of injustice and pressure, let us follow the midwives' example, fearing God and acting wisely and rightly, trusting that he watches over his people and prepares deliverance even in the midst of suffering.

chapters.summary: Moses was born and hidden, then adopted by Pharaoh's daughter, and as an adult he fled to Midian after killing an Egyptian who was abusing a fellow Hebrew, where he helped Jethro's daughters at a well.
keyPoints: Moses was born, hidden by his mother for three months, and then placed in a basket among the reeds by the riverbank.
Pharaoh's daughter found and adopted Moses, and his own mother was brought in to nurse him.
Seeing an Egyptian mistreating a Hebrew, Moses killed the Egyptian and was forced to flee to Midian.
chapters.application: Even in difficult circumstances, God is quietly at work preparing us. Let us trust in his sovereignty, learn patience while we wait, and believe he will lead us into what he has appointed for us.

chapters.summary: God appeared to Moses in a burning bush, called him to lead Israel out of Egypt, and revealed his name to him.
keyPoints: Moses saw a bush burning at Horeb that was not consumed, and God called to him from within it.
God identified himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, come to rescue his suffering people.
God sent Moses to Pharaoh, promising to be with him, and revealed his name, I AM WHO I AM.
chapters.application: Even in the midst of an ordinary day, God may appear to us in unexpected ways. Let us learn to listen for his voice, trust his promises, and answer his call with courage, knowing he will be with us.

chapters.summary: Moses tried to excuse himself from God's call out of fear, so God gave him miraculous signs and sent Aaron to work alongside him, and Moses finally set out for Egypt in obedience.
keyPoints: Moses objected that the people would not believe him, so God answered with signs, turning his staff into a snake and his hand leprous.
God appointed Aaron to speak for Moses, and the two worked together to deliver God's message to Israel.
Moses set out with his family, but was confronted by God on the way for not circumcising his son, a crisis resolved when Zipporah acted, after which they continued on.
chapters.application: When you feel too weak for what God is calling you to, remember that he provides both partners and proof. Simply trust and obey, and he will accomplish his purpose.

chapters.summary: Moses and Aaron made their first request to Pharaoh to let the Israelites go, but he refused and increased their workload, plunging the people into even deeper suffering.
keyPoints: Moses and Aaron delivered God's command to Pharaoh, asking that Israel be allowed to hold a feast in the wilderness.
Pharaoh not only refused but accused the Israelites of laziness and increased their workload.
The suffering people complained against Moses and Aaron, and Moses in turn questioned God.
chapters.application: When obeying God leads to greater hardship, do not lose heart. Trust that his purposes will surely be fulfilled, and seek his guidance in prayer.

chapters.summary: The LORD reaffirmed his promise to the Israelites and sent Moses and Aaron to speak to Pharaoh, but the people would not listen, and Moses again pleaded that he was not eloquent enough.
keyPoints: God reaffirmed the covenant he made with Abraham and the other patriarchs, promising to rescue Israel from slavery in Egypt.
Moses relayed God's words to the Israelites, but they would not listen because of their discouragement and cruel labor.
The LORD commanded Moses and Aaron to go to Pharaoh; Moses pleaded that he was unskilled in speech, but God sent him anyway.
chapters.application: When we face hardship and feel inadequate, let us remember that God's promises never change. He will accomplish his purposes; we need only obey and trust him.

chapters.summary: God sent Moses and Aaron to speak to Pharaoh and performed the sign of Aaron's staff turning into a snake, but Pharaoh's heart was hard and he refused to listen.
keyPoints: God made Moses like God to Pharaoh, with Aaron serving as his spokesman.
Aaron's staff turned into a snake and swallowed the staffs of Egypt's magicians, displaying God's power.
Pharaoh's heart was hard, and he would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had said.
chapters.application: When facing a stubborn situation, trust in God's power and faithfully speak his word, for he rules over all things and will accomplish his purpose.

chapters.summary: Through Moses and Aaron, God sent the plagues of frogs, gnats, and flies to display his power and show that he is the LORD who would set Israel free.
keyPoints: God told Moses to have Aaron stretch out his staff, bringing up frogs until they covered the land of Egypt.
Pharaoh begged Moses to pray away the frogs, but afterward hardened his heart again and refused to let Israel go.
God sent the plagues of gnats and flies, showing his own finger at work and a clear distinction for his people, yet Pharaoh remained hard-hearted.
chapters.application: When we witness God's evident work, let us respond with humility and obedience, turning back to him quickly rather than hardening our hearts like Pharaoh and losing the chance to receive his grace.

chapters.summary: God sent the plagues of pestilence, boils, and hail, and though Pharaoh's heart remained hard, God's power was clearly displayed.
keyPoints: God struck Egypt with pestilence, but Pharaoh's heart remained hard and he still refused to release Israel.
Moses threw ashes into the air, bringing boils on the Egyptians, but Pharaoh would not heed the warning.
God sent a devastating hailstorm, sparing only Goshen, where the Israelites lived, under his protection.
chapters.application: When we face difficulties, let us remember that God is in control of everything. He protects those who trust him, and we should submit to his will rather than hardening our hearts.

chapters.summary: Moses and Aaron brought the eighth and ninth plagues before Pharaoh, but his heart remained hard and he still would not let Israel go.
keyPoints: God sent a plague of locusts that covered the land and devoured every plant and all the fruit of the trees.
Pharaoh confessed his sin and begged for mercy, but once the plague lifted his heart hardened again and he refused to release the people.
God sent a plague of darkness that covered Egypt for three days, while the Israelites had light where they lived.
chapters.application: When we go through hardship, let us remember that God is sovereign over all things and can turn darkness into light. Let us trust him rather than letting our circumstances harden our hearts.

chapters.summary: God announced the final and most severe plague, the death of every firstborn in Egypt, and instructed the Israelites to prepare to leave.
keyPoints: God told Moses that he would harden Pharaoh's heart once more before finally letting Israel go.
Moses announced the tenth plague: every firstborn son and firstborn animal in Egypt would die.
God promised that the Israelites could ask the Egyptians for articles of silver and gold, and Moses was held in great honor before Pharaoh.
chapters.application: God will surely fulfill his promises. Let us wait on him in faith and prepare ourselves to obey his leading, even when circumstances seem difficult.

chapters.summary: God instituted the Passover, instructing the Israelites to slaughter a lamb and apply its blood to their doorframes so the destroying angel would pass over them, delivering them from slavery in Egypt.
keyPoints: God appointed the fourteenth day of the first month as the Passover, with the lamb foreshadowing redemption.
Blood applied to the doorframes caused the destroying angel to pass over, protecting the Israelites.
The Israelites left Egypt that very night after the plague struck the firstborn of Egypt and Pharaoh was forced to let them go.
chapters.application: Let us remember God's deliverance and give thanks that Christ is our Passover Lamb, trusting in his protection and guidance each day.

chapters.summary: This chapter records how, after the Israelites left Egypt, God instructed them to consecrate every firstborn to him and to observe the Passover, and led them with a pillar of cloud and a pillar of fire.
keyPoints: Every firstborn was to be consecrated to God, in remembrance of how he delivered Israel out of Egypt.
The Feast of Unleavened Bread was to be kept as a lasting ordinance, with no leavened bread eaten for seven days.
God led the people day and night by a pillar of cloud and a pillar of fire, guiding them through the wilderness.
chapters.application: Let us remember God's salvation and consecrate ourselves to him, trusting his guidance through the wilderness of life, for whether by day or by night, he is with us.

chapters.summary: The Israelites crossed the Red Sea and the pursuing Egyptian army was drowned, as God displayed his mighty power to save his people.
keyPoints: God directed the Israelites to turn back and camp, leading Pharaoh to think they were lost and pursue them.
Moses told the people not to be afraid but to watch the LORD fight for them.
God parted the Red Sea so the Israelites crossed on dry ground, while the Egyptian army was drowned in the returning waters.
chapters.application: When facing hardship, do not struggle in your own strength. Be still and trust in God, for he will open a way for you and show his salvation and faithfulness.

chapters.summary: After crossing the Red Sea, Moses and Miriam led the people in song, praising God for his power and salvation.
keyPoints: Moses and the Israelites sang a song praising God for triumphing over the Egyptian army.
Miriam led the women in playing tambourines and dancing in response to God's deliverance.
When the people encountered bitter water in the wilderness, God showed Moses how to make it sweet and established a statute of healing there.
chapters.application: When we experience God's salvation, let us respond with songs and thanksgiving, and trust in his healing and provision even in times of hardship.

chapters.summary: In the wilderness the Israelites grumbled from hunger, so God sent down manna and quail from heaven, instructing them to gather only enough for each day, twice as much on the sixth day, and to rest on the seventh.
keyPoints: The people grumbled against Moses and Aaron out of hunger, and God promised to provide food.
God provided manna and quail, showing his faithfulness and care.
God taught the people to keep the Sabbath, gathering a double portion of manna on the sixth day.
chapters.application: Lack is an unavoidable part of life, but God provides in his own time. Let us learn to trust him day by day rather than hoarding out of anxiety, and find his peace and grace in rest.

chapters.summary: At Rephidim the Israelites grumbled for lack of water, so Moses struck the rock as God instructed and water came out, and afterward they fought the Amalekites and won by God's help.
keyPoints: Lacking water, the people quarreled with Moses, nearly stoning him, so he cried out to God.
God told Moses to strike the rock with his staff, and water flowed out, solving the crisis.
The Amalekites attacked; Moses prayed with hands raised while Joshua led the army into battle, and Israel won.
chapters.application: When life brings hardship, do not grumble. Follow Moses' example and cry out to God, trusting that he will provide what we need and grant victory over every challenge.

chapters.summary: Moses was reunited with his father-in-law Jethro, who offered sacrifices and advised Moses to appoint judges to share the burden of leadership.
keyPoints: Moses told his father-in-law about all God's wonderful acts in delivering Israel from Egypt, and Jethro gave glory to God.
Seeing Moses judging the people alone, Jethro pointed out that the burden was too heavy and advised appointing leaders over thousands and other divisions.
Moses adopted the advice and set up a system of judges, so the people received timely justice and Moses was freed to focus on greater matters.
chapters.application: Let us learn to humbly accept good advice from others rather than carrying every burden alone, working together as a team so that everyone benefits and we ourselves find rest.

chapters.summary: The Israelites arrived at Mount Sinai, where God made a covenant with them, gave them the law, and appeared in fire, filling the people with awe.
keyPoints: In the third month after leaving Egypt, the Israelites came to the Wilderness of Sinai and camped before the mountain.
Through Moses, God declared that if the people kept his covenant, they would become a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.
God descended on Mount Sinai in thunder, lightning, and a thick cloud, warning the people not to break through to approach it.
chapters.application: Though we do not live under the awesome majesty of Mount Sinai today, we should still draw near to God with reverence, keep his word, and live as a holy witness.

chapters.summary: God gave the Ten Commandments at Mount Sinai, establishing his covenant relationship with Israel and teaching them how to worship God and treat one another.
keyPoints: God personally gave the Ten Commandments as the core law of his covenant with his chosen people.
The Ten Commandments cover both the worship owed to God and our responsibilities toward one another.
The commandments emphasize the enduring nature of the covenant and God's promise to those who love him.
chapters.application: The Ten Commandments are God's loving guide for living in true freedom. Today let us obey his word with grateful hearts, living out love and justice in our families and communities.

chapters.summary: This chapter records the ordinances God gave Israel through Moses concerning servants, injuries, and restitution, revealing God's justice and compassion.
keyPoints: A Hebrew servant was to serve six years and go free in the seventh, though one who loved his master could choose lifelong service.
The chapter sets penalties for fatal injuries as well as serious offenses such as striking one's parents or kidnapping.
Laws of restitution, such as for an ox that gores someone or an uncovered pit, reflect the principle of fair responsibility.
chapters.application: God cares about fairness in society and the dignity of every person. Let us respect others in daily life and take responsibility for our actions with love and justice.

chapters.summary: This chapter records laws concerning restitution, morality, and compassion, teaching Israel how to live out holiness and justice in daily life.
keyPoints: Theft or damage to another's property required double restitution, reflecting the principle of fairness.
The law protected the vulnerable, such as foreigners, orphans, and widows, revealing God's compassionate heart.
Charging interest on loans and cursing rulers were forbidden, emphasizing social order and the fear of God.
chapters.application: In our daily dealings, let us be honest and trustworthy, make restitution for any loss we cause, and actively care for those in need around us, putting God's justice and compassion into practice.

chapters.summary: This chapter records detailed laws God gave through Moses covering fair judgment, the sabbatical year, the three annual festivals, and promises and warnings regarding entering Canaan.
keyPoints: The people were not to follow the crowd in doing wrong, to testify fairly in disputes, and not to show favoritism to the poor.
They were to observe the sabbatical year and the Sabbath day, giving both the land and the people rest.
Three times a year they were to keep a feast to the LORD, and never appear before him empty-handed.
chapters.application: In daily life, let us treat others fairly and without partiality, and set aside time to rest and worship God, enjoying the rest and provision he gives.

chapters.summary: God made a covenant with Israel, and Moses sprinkled blood on the people to seal the covenant relationship.
keyPoints: God called Moses, Aaron, and others up the mountain, but only Moses was permitted to draw near to God.
Moses read the Book of the Covenant aloud, and the people twice responded that they would obey all God's words.
Moses sprinkled blood on the people as a sign of the covenant, then went up the mountain to receive the tablets of stone.
chapters.application: Though we today do not experience a ceremony of sprinkled blood, we are joined to God in covenant through the blood of Christ. Let us obey God's word with grateful hearts and live as people of his covenant.

chapters.summary: This chapter records God's instructions to Moses for gathering offerings to build the tabernacle and its furnishings, and gives detailed specifications for the ark of the covenant, the table for the bread of the Presence, and the lampstand.
keyPoints: God commanded the Israelites to bring a freewill offering for building the sanctuary.
The chapter describes in detail the dimensions, materials, and mercy seat of the ark of the covenant, symbolizing God's presence.
It sets out the making of the table for the bread of the Presence and the lampstand, signifying God's provision and light.
chapters.application: Let us give our time, talents, and resources willingly to build up the church, and through prayer and Scripture reading experience God's presence and light.

chapters.summary: This chapter gives detailed instructions for building the tabernacle, including the curtains, frames, bars, and the veil that divided its sections, emphasizing that it must be built exactly according to the pattern God showed.
keyPoints: Ten curtains of fine linen and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, embroidered with cherubim, were to be made.
Acacia wood frames overlaid with gold, along with silver bases and bronze bars, gave the tabernacle its stability.
A veil separated the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place, where the ark of the covenant was placed.
chapters.application: Let us live with reverence, according to God's will, letting Christ be the foundation of our lives, united in the Spirit, so that we become a dwelling place for God's glory.

chapters.summary: This chapter records the specifications for building the altar and the courtyard of the tabernacle, emphasizing the holiness and order of worship.
keyPoints: The altar was made of acacia wood overlaid with bronze, fitted with a network and rings for carrying.
The courtyard was enclosed with fine linen curtains and bronze bases, with an embroidered screen for its entrance.
The lamp was to burn continually from evening until morning on pure olive oil, tended by Aaron and his sons.
chapters.application: Our service must be carried out according to God's will, sustained by continual prayer and the light of his presence, so that worship becomes part of our everyday life.

chapters.summary: This chapter gives detailed instructions for making the priestly garments, including the ephod, the breastpiece, and the robe, and directs that Aaron and his sons be anointed as priests.
keyPoints: Sacred garments were to be made for glory and beauty, setting Aaron apart as holy.
The ephod was made of gold thread and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, along with fine linen.
The breastpiece bore twelve precious stones engraved with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel.
chapters.application: Though we are not priests, we are all called to be holy vessels. Let us serve God with reverence, and carry others in our hearts, just as the high priest carried the names on his breastpiece.

chapters.summary: This chapter details the ordination ceremony that set Aaron and his sons apart as priests, including sacrifices, washing, vesting, and anointing, and establishes the daily burnt offering, showing that God would dwell among the Israelites.
keyPoints: The priests were to be washed with water, clothed in sacred garments, and anointed, symbolizing cleansing and being filled with the Spirit.
A sin offering, a burnt offering, and a ram of ordination were offered, with blood applied to the altar and to the priests, signifying forgiveness of sin and consecration.
A burnt offering was to be made every morning and evening, symbolizing continual worship and devotion, and God promised to meet with his people at the tabernacle.
chapters.application: Though we no longer need to repeat these sacrifices today, we can offer ourselves daily through prayer and Scripture reading, living holy lives and experiencing God's presence.

chapters.summary: This chapter records instructions for making the altar of incense, the bronze basin, and the holy anointing oil, emphasizing holiness in worship and the priests' need for purity.
keyPoints: A gold altar of incense was to stand before the veil, with incense burned on it daily, symbolizing prayer rising to God.
A bronze basin was placed between the tabernacle and the altar, where the priests were to wash their hands and feet before serving.
The holy anointing oil and incense were to be made exactly as instructed and set apart, never imitated, showing God's holiness.
chapters.application: Drawing near to God each day requires first cleansing ourselves. Let our prayers rise like incense, offered with reverence, so that our lives become a fragrant offering.

chapters.summary: God appointed Bezalel and Oholiab to build the tabernacle and reaffirmed the Sabbath as holy, a sign for all generations.
keyPoints: God filled Bezalel with his Spirit, giving him wisdom, understanding, and knowledge to perform every kind of skilled work.
God appointed Oholiab to work alongside him, and gave skill to all who were gifted, so the tabernacle could be completed.
God reaffirmed the Sabbath as a sign of the covenant, declaring that anyone who profaned it must be put to death.
chapters.application: Each of us has gifts God has given us, and we should use them willingly in service. At the same time, let us remember to rest even amid our busyness, drawing near to God and finding true rest.

chapters.summary: At the foot of Mount Sinai the Israelites cast a golden calf; Moses shattered the tablets in anger, the Levites struck down the rebellious, God intended to destroy the people, but Moses interceded and God relented from the disaster.
keyPoints: When the people saw that Moses delayed coming down the mountain, they gathered and demanded that Aaron make them a god; Aaron cast a golden calf, and the people offered sacrifices and reveled.
God's anger burned against the people and he intended to destroy them, but Moses pleaded with him to remember his promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, and God relented.

Moses came down and saw the golden calf, shattered the tablets in anger, burned the calf, confronted Aaron, and called for those loyal to God, whereupon the Levites struck down about three thousand people.
chapters.application: When our patience runs out while we wait, let us stay alert and never replace true worship of God with worldly substitutes. Let us follow Moses' example, interceding in prayer for those who rebel and standing firm in God's truth.

chapters.summary: Because the Israelites worshiped the golden calf, God withdrew from them for a time, and Moses met with God face to face in the tent of meeting, asking him to go with them and to show his glory.
keyPoints: God told the Israelites to leave Mount Sinai, but because of their stubbornness he was unwilling to go with them himself, lest he destroy them.
Moses pitched the tent of meeting outside the camp, where the people sought God, and Moses spoke with God face to face, as one speaks with a friend.
Moses asked God to go with them and show his glory; God promised Moses he would see his back, but not his face.
chapters.application: Though we cannot see God today, we can experience his presence through prayer and Scripture reading. Let us ask him to guide us each day and long to know more of his glory.

chapters.summary: God gave new tablets of stone, declared his mercy and justice, and renewed his covenant with Israel, requiring that they worship him alone.
keyPoints: God told Moses to cut new stone tablets and wrote the Ten Commandments on them again, showing his grace and faithfulness.
God proclaimed his own character: compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness.
God renewed the commandments of the covenant, especially the command to worship the one true God alone and never bow to idols.
themes: Worship of the one true God
chapters.application: Today we too may come confidently before God, for he is full of mercy and grace. Let us worship him with pure hearts, stay far from idols, and experience his faithful presence.

chapters.summary: Moses relayed God's commands, calling the people to keep the Sabbath and to give freewill offerings for building the tabernacle and everything in it.
keyPoints: Moses reaffirmed the Sabbath commandment, stressing six days of work followed by a holy day of rest on the seventh.
He called the people to give freely, and anyone whose heart moved them was welcome to bring an offering.
He listed in detail the materials needed for the tabernacle and noted that God had already called Bezalel and Oholiab and given them wisdom.
chapters.application: Today, let us respond to God's grace with grateful hearts, giving our time, talents, and resources willingly to the work of the church, and keeping the Sabbath rest to draw near to him.

chapters.summary: This chapter records how the Israelites gave willingly and generously, and how Bezalel, Oholiab, and other craftsmen built the tabernacle according to God's instructions, receiving so much that they had more than enough.
keyPoints: The people gave so willingly and abundantly that Moses had to command them to stop bringing offerings.
Bezalel, Oholiab, and other skilled craftsmen, gifted with wisdom by God, made every part of the tabernacle.
The tabernacle's curtains, frames, and bars were all carefully made according to the pattern God had shown.
chapters.application: Whatever we give to God's work should come from a willing heart. He will supply the wisdom and ability needed, so that every offering becomes something useful in his hands.

chapters.summary: This chapter describes in detail how Bezalel, following God's instructions, made the ark of the covenant, the mercy seat, the golden lampstand, and other furnishings for the sanctuary, displaying God's presence and glory.
keyPoints: Bezalel made the ark of the covenant from acacia wood, overlaid it inside and out with gold, and cast four gold rings for it.
He hammered out the mercy seat and two cherubim from pure gold, facing each other above the mercy seat.
He made the golden lampstand, its snuffers, and its trays, all of pure gold.
chapters.application: In our ordinary work, let us complete what God has entrusted to us with faithfulness and skill, so that his presence is made visible in every detail of our lives.

chapters.summary: This chapter details the making of the tabernacle furnishings, including the altar, the bronze basin, and the courtyard, and records the amount of gold, silver, and bronze the people contributed.
keyPoints: Bezalel made the altar of burnt offering from acacia wood overlaid with bronze, along with a bronze grating and poles.
He made the bronze basin and its stand from the bronze mirrors of the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The courtyard curtains, posts, and bronze bases were all completed according to God's instructions, and the metals given were carefully recorded.
chapters.application: God takes note of all our offerings and labor. Let us give willingly in the work of the church, serve according to his will, and trust that he will accept it and bless it.

chapters.summary: This chapter records in detail how the Israelites made the priestly garments and the tabernacle furnishings according to God's instructions, completing all the work, and Moses blessed them.
keyPoints: The ephod and breastpiece were made of gold thread and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, reflecting holiness.
The priest's tunic, turban, and sash were carefully made according to God's instructions.
All the work on the tabernacle furnishings was completed; Moses inspected it and blessed the people, showing that their work was accepted.
chapters.application: When the work of our hands is done according to God's will, it will be accepted. May we obey God in all things, be clothed with holiness, serve faithfully, and enjoy his blessing and presence.

chapters.summary: The LORD instructed Moses to set up the tabernacle and anoint all its furnishings, Aaron and his sons were consecrated as priests, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
keyPoints: Moses set up the tabernacle exactly as God commanded and arranged all the holy furnishings within it.
He anointed the tabernacle and its furnishings to consecrate them, and Aaron and his sons were ordained as priests.
A cloud covered the tabernacle, and the glory of the LORD filled it, guiding the Israelites onward.
chapters.application: Let us live according to God's will, so that his presence fills our homes, making them today's tabernacle, a place where we worship him wherever we are.
